acceptance_criteria: A successful baseline followed by one or more failed marker reads and unchanged recovery emits no message, chat, access, or feed domain invalidations.
A failed observation preserves the last successful per-instance marker snapshot and emits at most one bounded unavailable transition plus one fresh recovery transition per failure episode.
Recovery with changed markers compares against the last successful snapshot and emits each necessary domain invalidation once.
A failed first observation remains distinguishable from a successfully observed first snapshot whose markers are null.
One unreadable instance does not suppress marker observation or publication for healthy peers.
Missing schema, lock or busy timeout, malformed result, closed handle, permission or storage failure, restart generation, repeated failure, and recovery are covered by focused negative tests.
Mutation tests fail if an unavailable result is converted to null markers or allowed to replace the last successful snapshot.
Availability events, logs, tests, and receipts use reserved synthetic markers and contain no database contents, locations, identities, credentials, messages, or raw exception text.
blast_radius: Fleet realtime marker observation, per-instance comparison state, WebSocket invalidation production, feed chronology, access and chat refreshes, recovery load, and any later sequence or reconciliation protocol that assumes producer events are truthful. No production database, transport, message, identity, service, process, or queue state was inspected or mutated.
evidence_summary: Two identical live captures established the issue identity, empty label state, timestamp, and body hash while SSH remote main remained at the pinned revision. At that revision, getSnapshot converts a typed getLatestMarkers failure into successful null markers; poll then compares those nulls with the prior successful markers, publishes message, chat, access, and feed invalidations, and stores the synthetic null snapshot. Unchanged recovery therefore appears to change both marker domains again. The surrounding catch cannot handle this path because no exception escapes getSnapshot. The two focused poller suites passed 24 of 24 tests, but none forces a typed marker-read failure; the green result confirms the stated coverage gap rather than the failure semantics. A fully paginated scan of 39 open pull requests and 1,333 changed-file records found four touched-path coordination overlaps, one direct documentation reference, and no open implementation owner for the marker-failure behavior.
falsifier_or_remaining_gap: A pinned-revision negative test that establishes non-null markers, returns ok=false, recovers to the same markers, and observes zero domain invalidations would falsify the source-derived reproduction. No such test exists. Full database fault injection, bounded availability-transition behavior, changed-marker recovery, restart generation, multi-instance isolation, mutation resistance, and downstream reconciliation remain implementation-time proof obligations.
impact: A transient marker-read failure is mislabeled as five domain changes, overwrites the last successful comparison point, and causes the same five false changes again on unchanged recovery. This pollutes operational chronology, forces needless client refetches, amplifies load during storage flaps, and can make a later reliable delivery protocol faithfully sequence false producer events.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read the live issue identity, body hash, labels, exact SSH main revision, and every overlapping pull-request head and file page immediately before registry integration or metadata mutation.
Keep the marker producer correction independent of issue #2519's delivery-continuity work while coordinating the shared generation and sequence contract.
Coordinate bounded observation failure classes with issues #2447 and #2514 without treating their taxonomy or request-time health scopes as ownership of realtime producer truth.
Run red and green focused tests for baseline, repeated failure, unchanged and changed recovery, first-observation failure, successful null markers, restart generation, and healthy-peer independence.
Verify content-free unavailable and recovered transitions cannot expose database paths, SQL, raw errors, messages, identifiers, credentials, or environment data.
Re-read the direct documentation reference from pull request #2516 and confirm it remains coordination evidence rather than an implementation owner.

suggested_remediation: Represent marker reads as typed available or unavailable observations, retain each instance's last successful snapshot across failures, and publish no domain invalidations for unavailable reads. Emit bounded content-free unavailable and recovered transitions once per episode; on fresh recovery compare against the last successful markers and coalesce only real changes. Add first-observation, repeated-failure, unchanged and changed recovery, restart-generation, healthy-peer, privacy, and mutation tests. Coordinate the failure vocabulary with #2447 and #2514 and the generation and sequence contract with #2519 without making either adjacent scope the implementation owner.
